answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 3 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the ripple gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the ember audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 48 variations of one paragraph as a result forfeits for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the velvet panel. That is 14 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
